state.claim: From 8th October the UK government will combine weekly flu and covid reports.

sources.text:
1 
 
Weekly national Influenza and  
COVID-19 surveillance report  
 
Week 13 report (up to week 12 data)  
1 April 2021

Weekly National Influenza & COVID-19 Report: week 13 report (up to week 12 data) 
2 
Executive summary 
This report summarises the information from the surveillance systems which are used to 
monitor Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19), influenza, and other seasonal 
respiratory viruses in England. References to COVID-19 represent the disease name 
and SARS-CoV-2 represent the virus name. The report is based on data from week 12 
(between 22 and 28 March 2021) and for some indicators daily data up to 30 March 
2021.  
 
Surveillance indicators suggest that at a national level COVID-19 activity remained 
stable in week 12 of 2021. There is currently limited testing for other respiratory viruses, 
however, laboratory indicators suggest that influenza activity is low.  
 
Rollout of the COVID-19 vaccination programme began in week 50. Social and physical 
distancing measures, including school closures, were introduced in week 1. Some 
measures were relaxed in week 10, including reopening schools. 
 
Overall case rates decreased slightly in week 12, however slight increases were seen in 
case rates in the 10-19 year age group in the past 3 weeks. This is likely to reflect 
schools reopening which occurred in week 10 and the mass testing programme in 
secondary schools. Overall Pillar 1 and Pillar 2 positivity remained similar to the previous 
week. Case rates were highest in Yorkshire and Humber. 
 
There have been increases in reported acute respiratory incidents in educational 
settings and care homes. SARS-CoV-2 was identified in the majority of these. The 
proportion of cases who are care home residents has been declining for several weeks. 
There have been small increases in some community and syndromic indicators of 
respiratory disease. 
 
Hospitalisations have been decreasing since week 2, and deaths with COVID have been 
decreasing since week 3. This continued decrease is likely to reflect the impact of social 
and physical distancing measures and the vaccination programme. 
 
COVID-19 vaccine coverage was 42.2% at the end of week 12, reaching over 90% in all 
cohorts over the age of 65 years and over 80% in all cohorts over 55 years. 
Hospitalisations and deaths are now falling more rapidly in the oldest age cohorts, which 
is likely to reflect the impact of the vaccination programme. The impact of the 
vaccination programme is also particularly notable in the seroprevalence data which 
indicates that around 46.4% of the population have antibodies to SARS-CoV-2 from 
either infection or vaccination, compared to 14.5% from infection alone. In the 70-84 
years age group around 93.5% had antibodies from either infection or vaccination 
compared to 4.7% from infection alone.

Weekly National Influenza & COVID-19 Report: week 13 report (up to week 12 data) 
3 
Through Respiratory Datamart, there was one influenza positive sample detected in 
week 12, which was an influenza B. Other indicators for influenza such as hospital 
admissions and GP influenza-like illness consultation rates remain low. Increases in 
rhinovirus activity were noted during the past 3 weeks.

Weekly National Influenza & COVID-19 Report: week 13 report (up to week 12 data)
